unit: O-009t / CMP-A09 — inactive/unpriced/free classification on the Foundation catalog
mode: candidate-only (no remote writes, no publish/deploy/entity ops)
source_of_truth: remote sandbox pulls taken this session; remote md5 re-verified unchanged after implementation

schema_finding.FoundationInventory.jsonc: no active/status/archived/free field. Deactivation in this estimator's context is `show_in_foundation === false` (schema default true).
schema_finding.LaborServiceInventory.jsonc: has `is_active` (default true, used in the page's service query) and `show_in_foundation` (default true, NOT in the query).
schema_finding.load_path: FoundationEstimator loads FoundationInventory with query {show_in_foundation:true} and LaborServiceInventory with {service_category:'concrete_service', is_active:true}, then merges normalizeConcreteSupplier rows client-side. A labor supplier carrying show_in_foundation:false therefore ENTERS the priced inventory flagged-but-present; a FoundationInventory row flagged false is filtered at the query and looks identical to a deleted row from inside the scan.

classification_contract.foundationCatalogRowAvailability(row): exported; 'deleted' tombstones (deleted/is_deleted/deleted_at/status in {deleted,removed,purged}) win over 'inactive' markers (show_in_foundation===false, is_active===false, active===false, archived/is_archived/disabled===true, status in {inactive,disabled,archived,discontinued,retired,deactivated}); else 'active'.
classification_contract.foundationItemCatalogAudit(item, invento: exported advisory mirror — per consumed basis emits {kind,index,componentId,field,inventoryId,selection:authored|unassigned|defaulted,availability:active|inactive|deleted|missing|unassigned,priceClass:priced|free|unpriced|override|deferred|unconsumed}. Non-blocking; nothing in it gates pricing.
classification_contract.issue_field_order: existence -> material_type (structural fit) -> lifecycle (inactive/deleted) -> consumed price basis. A wrong-type row was never a valid selection so type beats lifecycle.

new_issue_codes.catalog_item_inactive: selected id resolves to a row carrying an inactivity marker — blocks via the existing catalogIssues channel; acknowledged snapshot retained through the unchanged calcItem/delivery holds.
new_issue_codes.catalog_item_deleted: selected id resolves to a present tombstone row (soft-delete markers).
new_issue_codes.catalog_item_unpriced: row resolves, right type, active — but the price basis the item actually consumes is absent/malformed/negative. Recorded 0 (deliberate free) never flags.
new_issue_codes.catalog_item_unassigned_default: an implicit default is consumed: pillar item with falsy pillar_rebar_size (ported `|| '#4'` pick), or a falsy project_concrete_type while a concrete_service supplier is selected (ported `|| '4000_ae'` mix pick, kind 'concrete_delivery' field 'project_concrete_type').
new_issue_codes.catalog_item_unassigned_extended: existing code, new emission sites — selected_concrete_id unassigned (item silently rides the first supplier's delivery catalog or prices concrete at $0) and selected_forming_id unassigned while include_forming (silently $0 material). Forming's flag is suppressed when custom_forming_rate is authored (custom replaces the catalog basis entirely).

consumed_basis_mirroring.selected_concrete_id: unpriced checked only for bagged_concrete rows when custom_concrete_cost_per_cy is not authored — mirrors calcItemCost `conc_cost`/`concreteBags` consumption; concrete_service rows defer to the delivery scan's mix/admix/fee checks (never duplicated).
consumed_basis_mirroring.selected_forming_id: unpriced checked on cost_per_unit only when custom_forming_rate is not authored (mirrors `forming_rate` `??` pick).
consumed_basis_mirroring.rebar (v1): size-matched row checked on cost_per_unit only when custom_rebar_cost_per_ft is not authored; the availability scan keeps the existing manualRebar (finite && >=0) gate, the unpriced flag uses the calc's authored (non-null) gate.
consumed_basis_mirroring.reinforcement_material.inventory_id (v2): availability classification added; price basis stays with the reinforcement module (never duplicated).

parity_notes.preserved_codes: catalog_item_unavailable / catalog_item_type_mismatch / catalog_item_ambiguous / catalog_item_unassigned keep their codes on the same conditions they previously covered; messages are refined to name the class (e.g. 'is unavailable — the catalog row may have been deleted or deactivated' keeps the 'is unavailable' substring the page's diagnostics render).
parity_notes.changed_code: pillar item with falsy pillar_rebar_size AND no #4 rebar row: was catalog_item_unavailable, now catalog_item_unassigned_default (the condition is unassigned-ness; the default row is absent).
parity_notes.new_blocking_flags: unassigned concrete, unassigned forming (no custom rate), implicit #4 pillar default, implicit 4000_ae mix default, inactive/deleted/unpriced resolved rows — all previously unflagged or lumped; all retain acknowledged-snapshot amounts via the unchanged item/delivery holds.

residual_gaps_documented_not_fixed: Sibling pricing checks (poleCalculator, wallCalculator, wallCapCalculator, foundationEquipmentBindings) own their own catalog_item_* emitters — a selected-but-inactive row still prices silently on those paths because the row resolves. They are separate owned units; foundationCatalogRowAvailability is exported for their adoption.

FoundationInventory rows marked show_in_foundation:false are query-filtered upstream, so referenced ones classify 'unavailable' (deleted-or-deactivated message) rather than 'inactive' — distinguishing requires an unfiltered catalog reference, a page/caller concern outside this file's ownership.

The mix-default flag fires on falsy project_concrete_type + a resolved service supplier regardless of shipped yards (volume math is the delivery scan's; flagging earlier than consumption is the honest posture).

normalizeConcreteSupplier mints cost_per_unit: row.default_rate || 0 — absent default_rate becomes authored free; noted in materials14 DESIGN as a normalizer-unit issue (O-008 tail), not changed here.

verification.method: esbuild bundle of REMOTE calc graph (foundationCalc, legacyFoundationCalc, wall/pole/cap calculators, equipment bindings, input validation, construction checks, landscape, geometry inputs, reinforcement model, normalization boundary) with the candidate substituted for foundationCatalogIntegrity.js and foundationReinforcementItemProjection stubbed to null (v1-only through calcProject; the v2 branch is exercised directly on foundationItemCatalogIssues).
verification.coverage: lifecycle classifier (9 inactive markers, 5 deleted markers, active), price classifier (free/unpriced/priced/negative/malformed), every new issue code firing + controls (override suppression, free-not-flagged, manualRebar gate, service-row deferral), parity cases (type_mismatch, ambiguous, unassigned rebar, missing rows), acknowledged-snapshot retention under the new flags, calcProject end-to-end (itemPricing.available, catalogIssues channel, delivery hold).
verification.fixture_audit: materials14 complete-before.json: cases 5,6,8-12,16,22 (blank mix + service supplier) and 21 (unassigned concrete) will diverge from recorded expectations by design — the recorded silent-default consumption is exactly what this unit flags. Case fixtures' selected rows are all priced+active otherwise. test-foundation-material-ui T3/T4 and the catalog-integrity suite use items:[] or fully-assigned priced rows — unaffected.
verification.no_message_regressions: the only exact-message assertion in the suite is 'Pole 1: selected catalog material is unavailable' — emitted by poleCalculator.js (untouched); the assembly-scan pole path keeps the same prefix too.
